author: Copilot
body:
`subscriptionPillConfig` no longer defines an entry for the `expired` subscription status, but `AccountSubscriptionStatus` still includes `expired` and the UI will silently omit the status Pill for expired accounts. Either restore the `expired` mapping (red/"Expired") or handle all possible `AccountSubscriptionStatus` values so the status indicator is consistently rendered.
```suggestion
  'free trial': { color: 'yellow', label: 'Trial' },
  expired: { color: 'red', label: 'Expired' },
```

author: Copilot
body:
`SlackWebhookCapability` is instantiated with `self.env_name`, but the capability's `__init__` currently takes no arguments. This will raise a `TypeError` during CDK synth. Either update `SlackWebhookCapability.__init__` to accept/use `env_name` (and ideally `region`), or remove the argument at the call site.
```suggestion
        self._capabilities.append(SlackWebhookCapability())
```

author: Copilot
body: SlackWebhookCapability fetches the webhook secret with `boto3.client("secretsmanager")` without an explicit `region_name`. Because this runs at synth time, it will rely on the deployer's ambient AWS region configuration and may not match where the secret actually lives (notably, webbff config references a us-west-2 ARN). Pass an explicit region (e.g., from EnvConfigBuilder / capability init) or fetch by ARN and derive the region to avoid missing/incorrect secrets.

author: Copilot
body:
SlackWebhookCapability now fetches/injects the Slack webhook URL at synth time, but `get_secret_refs()` still returns the Slack secret ref. In EnvConfigBuilder this adds a `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` IAM permission for the runtime Lambda even though runtime secret access should no longer be required. Consider returning an empty list here (or only including the ref when a runtime-secret fallback is intentionally supported) to keep IAM least-privilege aligned with the new synth-time injection approach.
```suggestion
        return []
```

author: Copilot
body: The new permission guard on POST /account/contact is implemented via a FastAPI dependency, but existing unit tests for `send_contact_message` call the handler directly and won't exercise the permission check. Add a test that hits the route through the FastAPI app (or explicitly tests `require_permission(PermissionKey.can_manage_licenses)`) to assert 403/ActionNotAllowed when the permission is missing and success when present.
